body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (1) 🔗 Cross-repo conflicts (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Role kits can rewrite the playbook by changing its case 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>Spool.stored_kit_playbooks (and kit._owner_warning) recognise only the exact names
>PLAYBOOK.toml and meta/PLAYBOOK.toml, so an entry such as playbook.toml, Playbook.toml or
>Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml passes _carries_no_playbook and the engine approves the apply. On a
>case-insensitive filesystem the apply's unzip -o writes that entry over the real playbook, which
>the apply then commits. The role can therefore raise its own max_architect_consults, drop a stop
>rule or change the kickoff without the human seeing it, which is exactly what H-075 was meant to
>stop.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/spool.py[R578-583]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7/files#diff-afef6fe420dcdc67164710839c508470d94b5a42c23284c4d8cbca7fe9a71221R578-R583) > >```diff >+ try: >+ with zipfile.ZipFile(self.kit_dir(kit_id) / f"{name}.zip") as archive: >+ names = set(archive.namelist()) >+ except (SpoolError, OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile, ValueError): >+ return None >+ return tuple(path for path in PLAYBOOK_PATHS if path in names) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The check is an exact set lookup against PLAYBOOK_PATHS. The kit judge already accepts that
>extraction folds case on some filesystems: _path_problem compares .git with part.lower(), and
>TOOLING_DIRS is "compared case-folded (.GIT is .git, .Claude is .claude, where the
>filesystem folds case)". No such folding is applied to the playbook names, so the new hold is the
>only check that ignores case-folding filesystems.
>
> > [src/hands/spool.py\[574-583\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/spool.py/#L574-L583) > [src/hands/kit.py\[388-424\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/kit.py/#L388-L424) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2283-2313\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2283-L2313) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The §43 hold detects a carried playbook by exact name, so a kit entry like `playbook.toml` or `Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml` is approved by the engine. On a case-folding filesystem it then overwrites the playbook in force. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/spool.py[574-583] >- src/hands/kit.py[873-900] > >## Recommended Fix >Compare each zip name with `name.casefold()` against `{p.casefold() for p in PLAYBOOK_PATHS}`, and return the entry name actually found. Apply the same case-folded match in `_owner_warning`. Add tests for `playbook.toml` and `Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml` being held. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/b1cbd300-c9c9-450a-a5a8-75fb851d03f8?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/b1cbd300-c9c9-450a-a5a8-75fb851d03f8)

2. Reviewers cannot verify the reported run 📘 Rule violation ✧ Quality
>
>Description >
> >
>The new meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md records only seven-character commit prefixes and summarizes the
>gate without embedding its raw output. Because the report is the artifact reviewers use to validate
>the tip and tool claims, they cannot independently match the cited commits, counts, or messages to
>the run.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md[R8-11]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7/files#diff-51890f17d626388c6a5ad3a762059347669a69138a497b9877a871984fa958e3R8-R11) > >```diff >+1b822a5. Gate: `./scripts/check` green three consecutive runs before every >+unit commit (U0 excepted, red as the kit made it); at the tip >+(38e44ee) 5047 tests, three consecutive green runs and a fourth with >+`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` in its environment. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Compliance rule 3255379 requires reports to include full commit SHAs, explicit counts, and verbatim
>raw outputs. The report provides a short tip SHA and test count but no full SHA or raw
>./scripts/check output, while the unit table also uses short SHAs.
>
> > Rule 3255379: [Include exact SHAs, counts, and raw outputs in reports](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3255379?state=active) > [meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md\[8-11\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md/#L8-L11) > [meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md\[15-24\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md/#L15-L24) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md` uses shortened commit identifiers and narrative test results without including the exact tool output, so reviewers cannot independently verify the reported run. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md[8-11] >- meta/FINAL-REPORT-27.md[15-24] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace shortened commit identifiers with full commit SHAs, retain explicit integer metrics for every reported check, and add clearly marked raw-output sections containing the verbatim output from each discussed tool invocation. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/018c7020-5097-44de-82c4-cf0a5493b712?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/018c7020-5097-44de-82c4-cf0a5493b712)
3. Holds with other causes show the playbook-owner reason ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>_announce_hold now always passes reason=self._owner_hold_reason(job), so every buttoned hold of
>a kit that contains a playbook gets §43's "a change of the playbook is the owner's" reason. That
>includes kits that _escalate_kits is about to deny for a §33 violation, and kits that
>_kit_bytes_unchanged refused because the hash did not match. In those cases the human sees
>Approve/Deny buttons with a wrong reason for the hold, and the real cause shows only in a separate
>stop message.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R2134-2136]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R2134-R2136) > >```diff >+ # §43: the reason of a hold whose stored kit carries the playbook names the >+ # path, wherever the engine publishes it — a paused pipeline's included. >+ outcome = self.hold(job, reason=self._owner_hold_reason(job)) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>_announce_hold(approved=False) is called from _escalate_kits (before the engine denies the kit),
>from _kit_bytes_unchanged on a sha mismatch, from the paused-pipeline path and from the
>kit_apply_problem path. Every one of those calls now goes through _owner_hold_reason, which
>looks only at whether the stored zip contains a playbook, not at why the hold is being published.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2111-2140\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2111-L2140) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2315-2327\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2315-L2327) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2329-2349\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2329-L2349) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2382-2389\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2382-L2389) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Every engine-published hold of a kit containing a playbook gets §43's reason, even when it is held or denied for a different cause (an escalation or a sha mismatch). > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[2111-2140] >- src/hands/playbook.py[2254-2256] > >## Recommended Fix >Add an optional `reason` parameter to `_announce_hold`, defaulting to None. Pass `owner_hold_reason(...)` only from `_release_kit`'s `_carries_no_playbook` branch, and from the paused-pipeline branch if §43 requires it there. Other callers then keep the gate's reason. Reuse the names `_carries_no_playbook` already read, rather than reopening the zip on the event loop. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
4. Paused playbook kits lose hold reasons ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>_owner_hold_reason reaches notifications only through _announce_hold, while defer_hold skips
>holds filed during a pause and startup republishes held jobs without a reason override. When either
>path handles a role-filed kit carrying a playbook, the human sees only apply <name>, not the
>playbook path and ownership reason.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R2134-2136]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R2134-R2136) > >```diff >+ # §43: the reason of a hold whose stored kit carries the playbook names the >+ # path, wherever the engine publishes it — a paused pipeline's included. >+ outcome = self.hold(job, reason=self._owner_hold_reason(job)) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Api.send files the hold after asking defer_hold; a paused pipeline makes that method return
>false, so the event listener publishes the event's generic reason directly. Startup likewise calls
>publish_hold(job) without an override, although the new override and owner-reason helper are
>available.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2087-2100\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2087-L2100) > [src/hands/api.py\[438-449\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/api.py/#L438-L449) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[861-879\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/daemon.py/#L861-L879) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[407-436\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/daemon.py/#L407-L436) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2315-2327\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/3ad66dd7898abd463a2e9ba7ba09851da4a1e601/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2315-L2327) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Playbook-bearing kits filed while the pipeline is paused, or republished as held after restart, bypass the new reason override and show only the gate's generic apply reason. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[2087-2100] >- src/hands/playbook.py[2134-2136] >- src/hands/daemon.py[407-436] >- src/hands/daemon.py[861-879] > >## Recommended Fix >Derive and publish the playbook-specific reason for qualifying architect-filed holds on immediate and startup publication paths as well as deferred publication. Preserve the gate's stored reason and add tests for a kit filed during a pause and one republished after restart. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
